title: Lānaʻi Fifth Street affordable housing project
summary: In April 2026, a member said the Lānaʻi project with the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands would clear the island's housing list. In January 2026 the council approved Resolution 26-4, a ground lease for a long-term affordable housing project on Lānaʻi, and filed the older Resolution 25-233 it replaced. The developer said a state funding application starts in February, with land control key.

timeline.text: A member said the Lānaʻi project with Department of Hawaiian Home Lands (DHHL) would clear the island's housing list.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: File Resolution 25-233: The council filed an older Lānaʻi ground lease resolution that Resolution 26-4 replaced.
A council member said the lease advances the goal of long-term affordable housing on Lānaʻi.
Resolution 26-4: The council approved a ground lease for a long-term affordable housing project on Lānaʻi.
The developer said a state funding application process starts in February, and land control is a key part of it.
A council member asked that the Lānaʻi study also look at keeping homes owner-occupied for good, and the sponsor agreed.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: A council member said Lānaʻi has not had an affordable housing project in 30 years.

timeline.text: A council member proposed $250,000 for a master plan and feasibility study for Fifth Street in Lānaʻi City.
